acceptanceCriteria.text: Queue mutations are keyed by spec identity (`specPath` or `slug`); transitioning an item to `in_progress` / `shipped` / `skipped` / `failed` updates that row in place and never appends a second row for the same spec.
A state write that would emit a duplicate row index or duplicate `slug` fails closed and surfaces the conflict instead of writing the file.
The reported item count equals the length of the Phase 2 selection and stays constant while items ship.
After a completed standard batch, the state table holds exactly one row per selected spec, and every row is terminal (`shipped`, `skipped`, or `failed`).
Resuming a `completed` state file re-dispatches zero already-`shipped` items (no phantom `pending` rows survive close).
The per-row `updatedAt` advances on each transition, and the run frontmatter `updatedAt` advances on every state write.
`STATE.md` documents the one-row-per-spec invariant and the fail-closed duplicate guard in the queue schema and Resume Policy.
`ws-spec-multi/evals/evals.json` covers the duplicate-row scenario, and `npm run test` plus `ws-check-harness` exit clean after the change.

negativeScenarios.text: A standard batch ships an item and the state table gains a second row for that slug (must fail AC1/AC4).
A write that would emit a duplicate index or slug succeeds silently (must fail AC2).
Reported `shipped/total` changes after the Phase 2 selection is frozen (must fail AC3).
A `completed` state file is resumed and re-dispatches an already-shipped spec (must fail AC5).
Frontmatter `updatedAt` still equals `createdAt` at close (must fail AC6).
`STATE.md` omits the one-row-per-spec invariant or the duplicate guard (must fail AC7).
`npm run test` or `ws-check-harness` fails after the change (must fail AC8).
